# Developer-Archetype Theory Foundations

**Status:** research capture (incubating). Seeds a future "theory registry" for a
citation-traceable developer-archetype assessment — OpenStory's answer to YC's
Paxel, but with every conclusion traceable upward to the literature that licenses
it (intellectual provenance), not just downward to the events (empirical provenance).

**Provenance of *this document*:** generated by the `deep-research` harness on
2026-06-20 (96 agents, 16 sources fetched, 75 claims extracted, top 25 verified by
3-vote adversarial check; 24 confirmed, 1 refuted). Every record below rests on a
**primary source** (originating author's own text or peer-reviewed article) with a
unanimous 3-0 vote unless noted. This is the dogfood: an assessment framework whose
own foundations are themselves verified and cited.

---

## The design payoff: a warrant-strength discipline (the connective tissue)

The methodology layer came back fully grounded, and it gives us the rule that keeps
citation from becoming scholarly theater.

**Toulmin (1958)** decomposes any argument into `claim ← grounds ← warrant ←
backing ← qualifier ← rebuttal`. Confirmed verbatim: the **warrant** is the bridge
justifying the leap from grounds to claim; **backing** is the evidence beneath the
warrant. That maps onto the registry directly:

| Toulmin part | Registry / assessment field |
|---|---|
| claim | the archetype/dimension verdict ("The Conductor") |
| grounds | the metrics + raw CloudEvents |
| warrant | the one-sentence reasoning linking metric → construct |
| **backing** | **the theory record (this registry) — the citation hook** |
| qualifier | confidence **+ warrant-strength tier** |
| rebuttal | conditions that would weaken the verdict |

**Cronbach & Meehl (1955)** supply the discipline for the qualifier. Construct
validation applies *precisely when* an attribute is not operationally defined; a
construct is admissible only if it sits in a **nomological net** whose laws touch
observables; and the interpretation must be **falsifiable** — verbatim,
*"Rationalization is not construct validation... cannot maintain his claim in the
face of recurrent negative results."* **Kane's** interpretation-use argument
explicitly invokes Toulmin and recommends making the whole argument explicit for
high-stakes decisions.

This licenses a **three-tier `warrant_strength` field** on every link from a metric
to a construct:

1. **`validated`** — the metric has nomological-net contact with observables that
   the construct's *own* literature endorses. (We currently have ~none. Be honest.)
2. **`analogical`** — defensible reasoning from theory to a session signal, but the
   theory measures Person/Product, not Process. (Most of ours.)
3. **`metaphorical`** — the theory frames the language but does not license the
   number. (e.g., the *name* "Conductor".)

**Hard rule surfaced by the research:** when a Person/Product typology (Sternberg,
Boden's *outputs*) is applied to OpenStory's **Process** signal (session events),
the warrant is **at most `analogical`, never `validated`.** OpenStory's distinctive
claim is that it measures Process (Rhodes' third "P") from session events — so the
gap between a Person/Product construct and a Process observable must always be
declared, never papered over.

## Verified registry records (primary-source, 3-0)

### Creativity & cognitive-style typologies

**Sternberg — Propulsion Model of Creative Contributions**
- Scholar/year: Robert J. Sternberg, **1999**
- Primary work: *"A Propulsion Model of Types of Creative Contributions,"* Review of
  General Psychology 3(2):83–100. <https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1037/1089-2680.3.2.83>
- Core claim: contributions differ not in **amount** but in qualitatively distinct
  **types**, classified by stance toward a field's prevailing paradigm (4 types
  accept current paradigms, 3 reject them). A canonical **"style, not score"** typology.
- `warrant_strength` for our use: **analogical** (Person/Product typology → Process signal).
- Lineage: 1999 paper defines **7 types**; `descends_from` → Sternberg & Kaufman
  (2001/2010) and Sternberg, Kaufman & Pretz (2003), which expand to **8**. Anchor
  the record to 1999; flag the expansion as an edge.

**Boden — Combinational / Exploratory / Transformational creativity**
- Scholar/year: Margaret A. Boden, ***The Creative Mind*** 1990 (rev. 2004); concise
  statement in *"Creativity in a Nutshell."*
- Primary/stable sources: SEP entry <https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/creativity/>;
  interaliamag.org reprint (the ResearchGate PDF intermittently 403s).
- Core claim: creativity = ideas/artefacts that are **new, surprising, and valuable**,
  via three routes — **combinational** (unfamiliar combinations of familiar ideas),
  **exploratory** (new ideas *within* a conceptual space), **transformational**
  (changing the space itself). Conceptual spaces are culturally inherited, not
  originated by one mind.
- Why it matters: the canonical **computational** creativity typology — built for AI,
  and the most natural fit for "what kind of move was this?" (gluing libraries vs.
  idiomatic work vs. new architecture).
- `warrant_strength`: **analogical** (measures Process/Product of ideas; our signal
  is the coding process — a defensible but unvalidated bridge).

**Amabile — Componential Theory of Creativity**
- Scholar/year: Teresa M. Amabile; 1983 theory, canonical restatement **HBS WP
  12-096, 2012**. <https://www.hbs.edu/ris/Publication%20Files/12-096.pdf>
- Core claim: four necessary components — three within the person (domain-relevant
  skills, creativity-relevant *processes*, intrinsic task motivation) + one outside
  (the social/work **environment**). Creativity = outcomes both **novel and
  appropriate** on a **heuristic** (open-ended) task. Central tenet: the **intrinsic
  motivation principle**.
- Why it matters: uniquely names a **Press (environment)** component alongside Person
  — relevant because a coding session *is* a person-in-an-environment-with-an-agent.
- **Over-claim guardrails (must encode):** (1) "creativity-relevant processes" was
  "creativity-relevant *skills*" in 1983; (2) the intrinsic-motivation principle is
  her most-disputed tenet — her own **"motivational synergy"** work shows some
  extrinsic motivators help. **Do not claim extrinsic motivators are always harmful.**

### Software-delivery-performance frameworks (the second axis)

**DORA / Accelerate**
- Authors/year: Nicole Forsgren, Jez Humble, Gene Kim — ***Accelerate: The Science of
  Lean Software and DevOps***, IT Revolution, **2018**. Academic grounding: Forsgren
  et al., *"A Taxonomy of Software Delivery Performance Profiles,"* **AMCIS 2020**
  (hierarchical cluster analysis, n=7,522).
- Core claim: four key metrics — deployment frequency, lead time for changes, change
  failure rate, time to restore service (two throughput, two stability).
- ⚠️ **REFUTED claim (vote 0-3) — a correction to my earlier assertion:** the four
  discrete tiers **Elite / High / Medium / Low** are **not** from the 2018 book and
  **not** a peer-reviewed result. They come from later annual *State of DevOps
  reports*; the academic AMCIS paper derived **three** empirical clusters. The
  registry must treat the 4-tier scheme as a **popular-reporting artifact**, and may
  ground "distinct performance profiles / throughput-stability co-movement"
  academically.
- **Session-observability boundary:** deployment frequency, change failure rate, and
  time-to-restore generally need **production/incident data** and are **not**
  observable from a single coding session. Only **lead-time-like** intervals and
  **activity/flow** signals are session-observable. This is a hard limit on the
  delivery axis for a Process-only observer.

**SPACE — multidimensional developer productivity (sibling to DORA)**
- Authors/year: Forsgren, Storey, Maddila, Zimmermann, Houck, Butler — *"The SPACE of
  Developer Productivity,"* **ACM Queue 19(1), 2021**, DOI 10.1145/3454122.3454124.
- Core claim: productivity is **multidimensional** and **cannot be captured by a
  single metric** — Satisfaction, Performance, Activity, Communication/collaboration,
  Efficiency/flow (use ≥3). Forsgren co-leads both DORA and SPACE → the "sibling"
  framing is sound.
- Why it matters: **the strongest delivery-side warrant for "style, not score."** An
  authoritative source explicitly cautioning against single-metric evaluation.

### Methodology of traceable assessment

**Toulmin — model of argument** — *The Uses of Argument*, 1958. Backing = the
citation hook; chained inferences (one claim becomes the next's datum) = the
genealogy hook. Verified via two peer-reviewed sources (PMC9796688, PMC12390866).

**Cronbach & Meehl — construct validity** — *Psychological Bulletin*, **1955**.
<https://meehl.umn.edu/.../036constructvalidityidx.pdf>. The nomological-net +
falsifiability discipline. `descends_from` note: later collapsed/unified by **Messick**;
critiqued by **Borsboom (2009)**, **Haig**. Cite 1955 as the origin record.

## Pass 2 results (2026-06-20) — 9 constructs verified, "Conductor" REFUTED

The second pass (103 agents, 21 sources, 25 claims verified, **0 killed**) confirmed
the remaining load-bearing constructs against primary sources. All are now in
[`theory-registry.json`](./theory-registry.json) (16 records total). Rhodes-frame
locus tags:

| construct | year | measures | kind | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kirton KAI | 1976 | person | style | adaptor↔innovator; **style independent of level** (the cleanest "style not score") |
| Rhodes Four Ps | 1961 | (the frame) | method | grounds the `measures` field itself |
| Guilford | 1950 | person | style | the founding move; divergent/convergent |
| Csikszentmihalyi — Flow | 1996 | **process** | degree | eligible for a *validated* warrant |
| Csikszentmihalyi — systems | 1988 | press | method | attribution only — re-verify before citing |
| Sawyer collaborative emergence | 2009 | **process** | degree | see refutation below |
| Kaufman-Beghetto Four-C | 2009 | person | degree | **degree, not style** → growth-edge axis only |
| Dietrich | 2004 | **process** | style | ⭐ process-locus *and* style → best-matched to our signal |
| DeYoung Openness/Intellect | 2014 | person | degree | analogical only |

> ⚠️ **"THE CONDUCTOR" IS REFUTED (not merely unconfirmed).** The archetype the
> prototype assigned leaned on Sawyer's collaborative-emergence work. The primary
> source (Sawyer & DeZutter 2009) places the **conductor-led orchestra at the
> PREDICTABLE / CONSTRAINED pole** — his explicit *counter-example* to creative
> emergence. Verbatim: *"a symphony orchestra performs from a score and is guided by
> a conductor"*; *"Social encounters… controlled by a single individual… are less
> likely to manifest collaborative emergence."* Grounding a "Conductor" archetype in
> Sawyer would **invert the author's meaning.** The name and its backing must be
> dropped or re-grounded. This is the traceability system catching a *conceptual*
> error in the archetype, not just a citation slip — exactly its purpose.

**The constructive pivot.** Of the 16 records, only **`boden-1990`** and
**`dietrich-2004`** are simultaneously **style-axis candidates** *and* **process-locus**
— the only two eligible for a `validated` (not merely analogical) style axis, because
OpenStory measures Process. Dietrich's deliberate↔spontaneous × cognitive↔emotional
2×2 is the strongest process-native foundation for a style axis matched to session
events. Kirton's adaptor↔innovator remains the best-validated *instrument* but is
Person-locus, so it can only ever be `analogical` for us.

## Still open (future pass)

- **TTCT** (Torrance) — what it operationalizes (fluency/flexibility/originality/elaboration) and its locus. Not verified.
- **BVSR** (Campbell 1960 / Simonton) — a Process-locus model that *could* be validated against our signal. Not verified.
- Is there a primary source that grounds a **leadership/orchestration** archetype in
  collaborative creativity (Sawyer's "group flow" conditions; distributed-leadership),
  or should that axis be dropped now that "Conductor" is refuted?

## Open questions

1. How to encode `warrant_strength` as a typed field on each lineage edge, and the
   exact rule that downgrades to `analogical` when Person/Product → Process.
2. Which specific session signals (eval-apply patterns, turn shapes, lead-time-like
   intervals) can legitimately serve as nomological-net observables for each archetype.
3. How to ground the O'Malley-style "history of thought" genealogy methodologically,
   as distinct from computational explanation/provenance (it did not itself surface a
   verifiable primary-source claim — it's a *method*, not a finding).
